extracted.intended_audience: federal agency HR officials, agency legal counsel, OPM staff, and federal employees affected by adverse action/excepted service determinations
extracted.subtask_description: Official OPM rulemaking text explaining statutory standards, definitions, and procedures governing adverse actions, excepted service schedules (including the rescinded Schedule F), appealability, and related civil service protections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Merit System Principles
rubrics_metrics.description: The CSRA codified fundamental merit system principles summarized here: 1. Recruit, select, and advance on merit after fair and open competition. 2. Treat employees and applicants fairly and equitably. 3. Provide equal pay for equal work and reward excellent performance. 4. Maintain high standards of integrity, conduct, and concern for the public interest. 5. Manage employees efficiently and effectively. 6. Retain or separate employees on the basis of their performance. 7. Educate and train employees if it will result in better organizational or individual performance. 8. Protect employees from improper political influence. 9. Protect employees against reprisal for the lawful disclosure of illegality and other covered wrongdoing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These principles frame how hiring, personnel actions, and exceptions should be interpreted and applied; they underlie protections such as veterans' preference, appeals, and prohibitions on political influence. They are the policy foundation for statutory rules and OPM regulation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appealability of Short Suspensions and Associated Procedural Protections
rubrics_metrics.description: Suspensions of 14 days or less are not directly appealable to the MSPB.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even though short suspensions are not directly appealable, an employee against whom such a suspension is proposed is entitled to certain procedural protections, including notice, an opportunity to respond, representation by an attorney or other representative, and a written decision. Agencies must follow these minimum procedural rights when proposing short suspensions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Thresholds Requiring More Rigorous Adverse Action Procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: More rigorous procedures apply before agencies may pursue removals, demotions, suspensions for more than 14 days, reductions in grade and pay, and furloughs for 30 days or less, if the subject of the contemplated action meets the definition of an 'employee' under 5 U.S.C. 7511(a).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Whether these procedures apply depends on whether the individual qualifies as an employee under 5 U.S.C. 7511(a) (i.e., satisfies the applicable probationary or length-of-service conditions). Agencies must follow the statutory procedures in chapters 43 and 75 when those thresholds are implicated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'Employee' Under 5 U.S.C. 7511(a)
rubrics_metrics.description: Under section 7511(a)(1), 'employee' refers to an individual who falls within one of three groups: (1) an individual in the competitive service who either (a) is not serving a probationary or trial period under an initial appointment; or (b) has completed 1 year of current continuous service under other than a temporary appointment limited to 1 year or less; (2) a preference eligible in the excepted service who has completed 1 year of current continuous service in the same or similar positions in an Executive agency, or in the United States Postal Service or Postal Regulatory Commission; or (3) an individual in the excepted service (other than a preference eligible) who either (a) is not serving a probationary or trial period under an initial appointment pending conversion to the competitive service; or (b) has completed 2 years of current continuous service in the same or similar positions in an Executive agency under other than a temporary appointment limited to 2 years or less.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This statutory definition controls when chapter 75 protections, including notice and appeal rights for certain adverse actions, attach. Durational and probationary conditions must be checked carefully when determining appealability and procedural entitlements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory Exceptions: 5 U.S.C. 7511(b) Excepted Categories
rubrics_metrics.description: Excepted from chapter 75 protections and rights to appeal are certain civil servants described in 5 U.S.C. 7511(b), including, among other categories, officers appointed by the President with the advice and consent of the Senate and other officers whom the President is permitted to appoint himself or herself. Also excepted are individuals 'whose position has been determined to be of a confidential, policy-determining, policy-making, or policy-advocating character.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Determinations as to exception must be made by: (A) the President for positions the President has excepted from the competitive service; (B) OPM for positions it has excepted; or (C) the President or the head of an agency for positions excepted by statute. These exceptions are aimed at noncareer political appointments and carry implications for accrued rights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Chapter 43 Performance-Based Action Process
rubrics_metrics.description: Chapter 43 of title 5, U.S. Code, was created as an additional process for empowering supervisors to address performance concerns; agencies may use chapter 43 in addition to chapter 75.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The decision of which chapter (43 or 75) to use to address performance concerns is left to the discretion of the manager tasked with pursuing the action. Agencies should apply chapter 43 procedures where appropriate per statute and agency policy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Property Interest in Continued Employment and Due Process Requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Through various enactments (chapters 43 and 75), certain employees with requisite tenure may earn a property interest in continued employment; for such employees, removal and other actions may be taken only 'for such cause as will promote the efficiency of the service.' Once a government requires cause for removals, constitutional due process protection will attach to that property interest and determine the minimum procedures by which a removal may be carried out.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any new law affecting removal of employees with an accrued property interest must comport with due process (see Board of Regents v. Roth and Cleveland Bd. of Education v. Loudermill). Agencies must ensure statutory and procedural protections meet constitutional standards before depriving incumbents of their property interests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Covered Position Definition for Prohibited Personnel Practices (5 U.S.C. 2302)
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Covered position' means any position in the competitive service, a career appointee in the Senior Executive Service, or a position in the excepted service unless 'conditions of good administration warrant' a necessary exception on the basis that the position is of a 'confidential, policy-determining, policy-making, or policy-advocating character.' At 5 U.S.C. 2302(a)(2)(A), Congress lists personnel actions that can form the basis of a prohibited personnel practice under 5 U.S.C. 2302(b). The CSRA codified a comprehensive list of prohibited personnel practices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Positions excepted from coverage of prohibited personnel practices are aligned with the long-understood category of political appointees; agencies should interpret 'covered position' consistent with statutory text and precedent.

rubrics_metrics.name: OPM Excepted Service Schedules (A–E) — Schedule A
rubrics_metrics.description: Schedule A—Includes positions that are not of a confidential or policy-determining character for which it is not practicable to examine applicants, such as attorneys, chaplains, and short-term positions for which there is a critical hiring need.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Schedule A is used where competitive examination is impracticable; agencies must still exercise selection 'solely on the basis of relative ability, knowledge, and skills' where applicable and follow any OPM-established qualification standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: OPM Excepted Service Schedules (A–E) — Schedule B
rubrics_metrics.description: Schedule B—Includes positions that are not of a confidential or policy-determining character for which it is not practicable to examine applicants. Unlike Schedule A positions, Schedule B positions require an applicant to satisfy basic qualification standards established by OPM for the relevant occupation and grade level. Schedule B positions engage in a variety of scientific, professional, and technical activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Schedule B allows hiring without competitive examination but with OPM-established basic qualification requirements; agencies must follow OPM qualification standards when using Schedule B.

rubrics_metrics.name: OPM Excepted Service Schedules (A–E) — Schedule C
rubrics_metrics.description: Schedule C—Includes positions that are policy-determining or which involve a close and confidential working relationship with the head of an agency or other key appointed officials. These positions include most political appointees below the cabinet and subcabinet levels.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Schedule C positions are the traditional mechanism for political appointments that are 'confidential, policy-determining, policy-making, or policy-advocating' in character; incumbents are not treated as career civil servants for purposes of chapter 75 protections.

rubrics_metrics.name: OPM Excepted Service Schedules (A–E) — Schedule D
rubrics_metrics.description: Schedule D—Includes positions that are not of a confidential or policy-determining character for which competitive examination makes it difficult to recruit certain students or recent graduates. Schedule D positions generally require an applicant to satisfy basic qualification standards established by OPM for the relevant occupation and grade level. Positions include those in the Pathways Programs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Schedule D supports internship/recent graduate recruitment (Pathways); agencies using Schedule D must observe the specific program rules and OPM qualification standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: OPM Excepted Service Schedules (A–E) — Schedule E
rubrics_metrics.description: Schedule E—Includes positions of administrative law judges.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Schedule E is narrowly tailored to administrative law judge positions and carries unique statutory/regulatory implications; agencies must treat Schedule E slots consistent with statutory authorities governing ALJs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Excepted Service Incumbent Protections and Probationary/Length-of-Service Conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: Competitive and excepted service incumbents, except those in Schedule C—and others excluded under 5 U.S.C. 7511(b)—become 'employees' for purposes of civil service protections after they satisfy the probationary or length of service requirements in 5 U.S.C. 7511(a. Excepted service employees, except those in Schedule C and others excluded under section 7511(b), maintain the same notice and appeal rights for adverse actions and performance-based actions as competitive service employees, though they must satisfy different durational requirements before these rights become available.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies must check which schedule an incumbent occupies and whether durational/probationary thresholds have been met before imposing adverse or performance-based actions that would trigger notice/appeal rights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Veterans' Preference Durational Requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: So-called 'preference eligibles' in an executive agency, the Postal Service, or the Postal Regulatory Commission must complete 1 year of current continuous service to avail themselves of the relevant notice and appeal rights.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Veterans' preference status affects the durational threshold for acquiring appeal rights; agencies must account for preference-eligible status when determining whether statutory protections attach.

rubrics_metrics.name: Senior Executive Service (SES) Distinct Procedures and Coverage
rubrics_metrics.description: The SES is a service separate from the competitive and excepted services with a separate system for hiring, managing, and compensating executives. The SES is governed by separate adverse action procedures in Subchapter V of chapter 75. The adverse action rights set out in Subchapter V (5 U.S.C. 7541–7543) apply only to career appointees to the SES. Removal of career employees for less than fully successful executive performance is governed by 5 U.S.C. 3592. Noncareer SES members are not affected by these protections and can be removed by an agency head.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When dealing with SES personnel actions, agencies must apply Subchapter V rules for career SES appointees and recognize noncareer SES appointees may be removable at will unless specific law provides otherwise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effects and Mechanics of Executive Order 13957 (Schedule F) as Described
rubrics_metrics.description: Executive Order 13957, 'Creating Schedule F in the Excepted Service,' would have risked stripping adverse and performance-based action grievance and appeal rights from large swaths of the Federal workforce by placing positions in a new excepted schedule (Schedule F), thereby subjecting incumbents to removal at will. The Order directed agency heads to review positions to identify those 'of a confidential, policy-determining, policy-making, or policy-advocating character,' petition OPM for placement in Schedule F (with specified timeframes), and purported to make veterans' preference apply only 'as far as administratively feasible.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OPM notes that Schedule F differed from prior excepted service precedents (which addressed unique hiring impracticability) by being broad and numerically unlimited, and that it would have allowed agencies to remove incumbents' accrued procedural rights. Agencies seeking to replicate such changes must observe statutory limits; OPM emphasizes existing mechanisms (chapter 43/75) that address management concerns without creating Schedule F-like effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedural Timeline for Agency Petitions Under EO 13957
rubrics_metrics.description: EO 13957 instructed agency heads to conduct an initial review and petition OPM by January 19, 2021 (the day before the Inauguration) to place positions within Schedule F; after that, agency heads had another 120 days to petition OPM to place additional positions in Schedule F.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This timeline shows the expedited and time-limited processes EO 13957 imposed on agencies; OPM observed that the Order sought rapid placement without prior determinations, which departed from prior practice where the excepted schedules were applied after a determination that competitive examination was impracticable.

rubrics_metrics.name: OPM's Construction of 'Confidential, Policy-Determining, Policy-Making, or Policy-Advocating' Phrase
rubrics_metrics.description: OPM construes the statutory language referencing positions of a 'confidential, policy-determining, policy-making, or policy-advocating' character as aligning with the longstanding understanding that such language equates to political appointees (typically those in Schedule C). OPM intends to define that phrase consistently with decades of practice and statutory reading of 5 U.S.C. 7511(b)(2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies should treat that phrase as referring to political appointments rather than to broad classes of career officials; this interpretation supports retaining accrued adverse action rights for incumbents moved involuntarily into excepted service unless statutory prerequisites for removal of those rights are met.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of Section 3302 'Conditions of Good Administration' Standard
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 3302 permits the President to make necessary exceptions of positions from the competitive service if 'conditions of good administration warrant.' That standard relates to whether positions should be excepted from the competitive service, but Congress did not suggest that the same standard authorizes removal of incumbents' accrued adverse action rights under chapter 75.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies and the Executive should not conflate authority to except positions from competitive procedures under section 3302 with authority to strip incumbents of statutory protections; OPM interprets section 3302 as about positional exceptions, not automatic removal of accrued employee rights.
